title: Dedicated: customer impact tracking + rollout comms for TP stability fixes (runtime-1.19)
creator: Paula Mendes
project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Overview
We have repeat customer-facing timeouts/hangs in multi-GPU tensor-parallel (TP) replicas under sustained load, most visible on Dedicated clusters (A100 80GB + high-throughput, streaming-heavy traffic). This PM ticket is the “customer layer” tracker: who is impacted, what we are telling them, and how we coordinate rollout comms + mitigations with CS/Support/SRE while Engineering ships stability fixes in runtime-1.19.

Primary goals
1) Maintain consistent, accurate messaging to affected Dedicated accounts during diagnosis + rollout.
2) Track customer impact (severity, scope, mitigation effectiveness) and ensure we close the loop post-fix.
3) Ensure Dedicated rollout sequencing (Dedicated-first) is aligned with SRE + Release mgmt and that Support has playbooks.

Non-goals
- This ticket is not the place to debug root cause (see ENG-4821 and linked sub-issues + design doc).
- We are not committing to performance improvements; the committed outcome is correctness/stability + better detection/mitigation.

Customer impact summary (as of 2025-03-03)
Symptoms customers report:
- Intermittent request hangs (especially streaming) leading to downstream timeouts.
- Elevated p99 / p99.9 latency during bursty concurrency, long context workloads.
- Occasional replica wedge that requires drain/replace.

Operational impact we observe:
- Autoscaling thrash during bursts as timeouts spike.
- Increased page volume due to correlated timeouts + replica drains.

Known affected segment:
- Dedicated accounts using multi-GPU per replica (TP=2/4/8) and mixed prefill/decode.
- Highest severity where streaming responses are critical (customer perceives “hung” UI).

- ACME AI (Dedicated, A100 80GB). Escalated via Support + CS.

Rollout plan alignment (Dedicated-first)
Source of truth for release mechanics: ENG-4829 (Release plan runtime-1.19 TP stability)
Target sequencing (subject to canary results / go-no-go):
- Canary 0: internal perf-canary + benchmark-lab stress scenarios (ENG-4828)
- Canary 1: 1–2 Dedicated clusters with opt-in debug logging window if needed (INT-2219)
- Canary 2: expand Dedicated rollout (top impacted accounts first) with feature flags
- Then: Hosted expansion

Messaging principles (keep consistent)
- Be precise: “stability fixes” not “performance improvements.”
- Avoid over-committing: use “targeting runtime-1.19 canary” language until go/no-go.
- Share mitigations proactively: concurrency caps / safe defaults / drain guidance.
- Acknowledge impact + provide a concrete next update time.

Customer-facing guidance (approved talking points)
What we know:
- Under certain mixed workloads on multi-GPU TP replicas, the runtime can enter a stalled state (compute vs comms vs scheduler starvation); this can manifest as streaming timeouts or apparent hangs.
What we’re doing:
- Shipping targeted stability hardening + stall detection (watchdog + safe abort/drain) and improved diagnostics.
What customers should do now:
- Apply temporary mitigations (see below) until runtime-1.19 is deployed to their cluster.
- Provide requested traces/logs only within agreed windows (we’ll coordinate with Support/SRE).

Temporary mitigations (Dedicated)
These should match the Support-facing doc: sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/tp-timeouts-workaround-dedicated.json
- Reduce max concurrency on impacted routes (preferably per-replica cap).
- Reduce batch size / disable aggressive prefill batching for long-context if set.
- Prefer shorter max output tokens for streaming endpoints during peak windows.
- If a replica appears wedged: drain + replace rather than letting traffic accumulate.
- If SRE approves: enable extra NCCL debug logging for a bounded time window (INT-2219) to capture stall signature.

Comms templates

Template A — Initial acknowledgement (email to customer)
Subject: Update on intermittent timeouts on Dedicated (multi-GPU TP)

Hi <Name>,

Thanks for the details you shared. We’ve identified a known stability issue that can occur under sustained load in multi-GPU tensor-parallel replicas, which can present as intermittent hangs/timeouts (often most noticeable with streaming).

What we’re doing:
- Our runtime team is actively working on targeted stability fixes and additional stall detection/diagnostics. These changes are planned for the next runtime release (runtime-1.19) with a Dedicated-first canary rollout.

What we recommend in the meantime:
- As a temporary mitigation, we can apply a concurrency cap on the affected routes / workloads and reduce batching aggressiveness during peak windows. This has reduced timeout rates for other Dedicated environments while fixes roll out.

Next steps:
- We’ll share a canary timeline for your cluster once we have the first canary results. We’ll also request a short, bounded window for additional logging if needed to confirm the stall signature.

We’ll send the next update by <Day/Time TZ>.

Best,
<CS/TAM name> + Redwood Inference


Template B — Canary enrollment / change notice
Subject: Dedicated canary: runtime-1.19 stability update (multi-GPU TP)

Hi <Name>,

We’re ready to canary runtime-1.19 on your Dedicated cluster to address the intermittent TP-related hangs/timeouts we discussed.

Change summary:
- Adds stall detection (watchdog) and safe abort/drain behavior to prevent long-lived hangs.
- Improves diagnostics and error surfacing to help distinguish comms vs scheduler stalls.
- Includes additional scheduler/comms hardening targeted at TP workloads under mixed prefill/decode.

Expected impact:
- Primary goal is improved stability and fewer request timeouts.
- We do not expect a user-visible performance regression; we will monitor p95/p99 latency and error rates during canary.

Schedule:
- Proposed window: <Date/time> (duration: <X> hours), with rollback criteria if error rate/p99 exceeds agreed thresholds.

If you approve, please confirm:
- Preferred window and point of contact for real-time validation.

Best,
<PM/CS name>


Template C — Post-canary summary (success)
Subject: Canary results: reduced timeouts on Dedicated (runtime-1.19)

Hi <Name>,

Sharing a quick readout from the runtime-1.19 canary:
- Observed: <timeout rate before> → <timeout rate after>
- p99 latency: <before> → <after> (within expected variance)
- Notes: <any remaining issues / mitigations still recommended>

Next steps:
- If these results hold for another <X> hours/day, we recommend proceeding to full rollout across your Dedicated cluster.

Best,
<PM/CS name>


Internal comms (Support macro snippet)
Use in Zendesk/Jira replies for SUP-48321/SUP-48344/SUP-48377 to ensure consistent language:
- “We’re tracking this as a known multi-GPU tensor-parallel stall scenario under certain mixed workloads. Engineering is shipping targeted stability fixes + better detection in runtime-1.19 with a Dedicated-first canary. In the interim, we recommend applying a concurrency cap and (if needed) draining/replacing replicas that appear wedged. We’ll provide a canary ETA once the first perf-canary gates pass.”

Coordination checklist (DRI: Lauren)
- [ ] Ensure Support doc is updated with current mitigations + what logs to collect (Confluence link above).
- [ ] Weekly (or as-needed) customer impact check-in with CS/TAM on ACME AI: timeouts, peak windows, mitigation adherence.
- [ ] Confirm with SRE whether extra debug logging is approved and for what window (INT-2219).
- [ ] Align with release captain on runtime-1.19 canary schedule + rollback criteria for Dedicated.
- [ ] After rollout: send post-change summary + confirm success criteria with customer.

Success criteria (customer-facing)
- Material reduction in streaming timeouts attributed to TP stall signatures (goal: near-zero hang-induced timeouts during peak windows).
- No increase in p99 latency outside agreed thresholds.
- Clear operational playbook: how to detect stall early + automated drain/mitigation behaviors are working.

Open questions / risks
- Watchdog thresholds: risk of false positives causing unnecessary drains; mitigate via feature-flagged rollout and careful threshold selection per model size (see runtime thread on default timeouts).
- Debug logging: NCCL debug can be noisy/overhead; must be time-boxed and approved.
- Customer expectations: ensure we don’t promise full elimination for all workloads until stress suite + canary are clean.
